name: Wisconsin
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. Wisconsin uses the last four completed quarters only if those do not qualify.
notModeled: The alternate base period: enter whichever four quarters the Department will use.
A claimant with an earlier benefit year must have earned 8 times the earlier weekly rate since it began.

citation.sourceDocument: Wis. Stat. §§108.02(4), 108.04(4)(a), 108.05(1)(r), 108.06(1); Wisconsin DWD, Qualifying Wages
citation.sourceNote: §108.05(1)(r): the rate is "4 percent of the employee's base period wages that were paid during that quarter" with the highest wages, "rounded down to the nearest whole dollar"; "if that amount is less than $54, no benefits are payable", and above $370 it is $370. So the high quarter must be at least $1,350. §108.04(4)(a): base-period wages of "at least 35 times" the rate, including "at least 4 times" it outside the high quarter, carried here as the lesser of 4 times and $1,480, which is 4 times the $370 maximum. §108.06(1): the total is the lower of "26 times the claimant's weekly benefit rate" and "40 percent of the claimant's base period wages". DWD: "The maximum WBR is $370." No dependent allowance; one unpaid waiting week. Chapter 108 as updated through 2025 Act 247. Read 2026-10-19.
